newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ok Tedi copper shipments resume in PNG.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ok Tedi copper shipments resume in PNG.

text.p: Copper shipments from the Ok Tedi mine in a remote arear of Papua New Guinea have resumed after being halted due to drought, the mine's operator, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Monday.
Shipments of copper concentrates by barge down the Fly River were suspended earlier this month because of low water levels, forcing the mine to meet deliveries from stockpiles in the Gulf of Papua.
"They started getting ships moving towards the end of last week," a BHP spokesman for the mine told Reuters.
"Depending on further follow-up rains, overall there is unlikely to be any interruption to shipments ... the river is a bit like a yo-yo, it goes up and down," he said.
He said cyclone Justin hovering off the coast of Australia's Queensland state tended to suck moisture from the river, contributing to periodic declines in the water level.
However, sufficient stockpiles of concentrates were on hand at the Gulf of Papua to meet at least two weeks' worth of deliveries, the spokesman said.
"We've got storage for another fortnight," the spokesman said.
Ok Tedi produces about 600,000 tonnes of copper concentrate annually. The material is typically shipped to destinations in Asia and Europe for smelting.

Concentrates are transported by pipeline from the mine to the port of Kiunga, and then by barge down the Fly River for loading onto a silo vessel in the Gulf of Papua before being transferred to waiting bulk freighters.
BHP owns 52 percent of the mine. The other partners are Canada's Inmet Mining Corp, with 18 percent and the Papua New Guinea government 30 percent.
